display.purpose: The big statement headline. Italic 400 on the marketing hero; roman 600 for the equivalent in-app heading. Fluid clamp on the .canon step.

headline.purpose: App page titles, section headers, empty-state and dialog titles. Zodiak bold roman 600 (.kirk), .paragon step. Marketing section headings take italic 400 instead.

title.purpose: Card titles and sub-section headers. Zodiak bold roman 600 (.kirk), .pica / .long-primer step. Botanical Latin inside is additionally italicised.

editorial-display-body.purpose: Long narrative-intro paragraphs set in Zodiak roman 400 (no .kirk), .long-primer / .primer size — e.g. a scheme's narrative_intro. Not a heading; the absence of .kirk is what separates it.

body.purpose: All running text. Inter 400, .primer step, line-height 1.5. Capped near 65ch with .o-measure. Colour is n-deep-grey, not ink.

body-sm.purpose: Secondary text, card subtitles, helper and hint copy. Inter 400, .brevier step.

caption.purpose: Metadata, timestamps, badge text; dense numeral columns with .o-type-tabular. Inter, .minion step.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, plate numbers, ALL field labels, status pills, botanical metadata. One class: .o-type-label (Spline Sans Mono, .minion, weight 500, uppercase, 0.14em). The earlier Inter small-caps variant on form fields is retired.

shadows.name: menu-raised
shadows.purpose: Popovers and the autocomplete menu. The one consolidated low step.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Lift on interactive cards on hover (also z-index:1) and on scheme frame panels. The raised step.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs only. The deepest step, for content that stops the page.

shadows.name: focus-ring-lavender
shadows.purpose: Button-component focus-visible ring, floated off the paper ground. Fields and menus instead use a 2px cyan outline.

motion.name: transition-default
motion.purpose: Token default (--transition-time-default). Colour/padding transitions on objects.

motion.name: transition-emphasis
motion.purpose: --transition-easing-emphasis. The one authored moment on a surface: the scheme-entry plate lift + engraving bloom, the scheme-scratch schedule row easing in as it is added. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible resting state; never for incidental hovers. Degrades to an instant state change under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: chat-typing
motion.value: opacity 0.3->1 + a 0.125rem rise, 1.2s ease, dots staggered 0.15s, infinite
motion.purpose: _chat.scss keyframe — the typing indicator's three dots while the assistant composes. The chat surface's one authored moment; static (opacity 0.55) under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: the-planting
motion.value: scheme-item-in (fade + -0.25rem settle) + scheme-card-wash (--_accent-wash -> white, 0.8s) + scheme-elevation-draw/-dot (stroke-dashoffset 1 -> 0, pathLength-normalised; dots bud a beat after their stem), all on the emphasis curve with a shared per-item --_delay
motion.purpose: _scheme-chat.scss keyframe family — the scheme workspace's one authored moment: one orchestrated response to a plant joining the scheme (its list card, its chat suggestion card, and its silhouette drawing up from the elevation's ground line). --_delay is 0 for a single add and staggered ~70–90ms per item when a populated sheet or fresh suggestion panel first arrives, so a scheme lands as a planting, not a dump. Every keyframe is animation: none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: micro-150
motion.purpose: Hardcoded in Button and .o-card--interactive for tight hover/press feedback. A known divergence from the 0.4s token.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every keyframe animation opts out here; spatial entrance/hover motion is also gated behind (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

motion.name: order-book-border-draw
motion.purpose: The order book's authored moment: each plant's silhouette in the letterhead draws up from the ground line on load (stroke-dashoffset on pathLength-normalised paths), flower heads budding a beat later. A plant added later draws alone, at once.

motion.name: order-line-in
motion.purpose: A newly added shopping list entry settling onto the sheet out of the add form's wash, while its silhouette draws into the border.

motion.name: order-resolve-in
motion.purpose: The resolve: when a name lookup comes back with a plant, its picture, name, common-name badges and summary settle in one after another.

motion.name: order-edit-in
motion.purpose: The rename form easing in where the entry's name stood.

motion.name: purchase-plate-in
motion.purpose: The plant's plate settling half onto the purchase dialog's dusk strip.

motion.name: order-shimmer
motion.purpose: While a name is being looked up: light across the entry's plate and across the two placeholder lines holding the summary's place. Incidental, looping; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: order-dots
motion.purpose: Three mulberry dots after 'Looking this up' and 'Adding it to your garden'. Static at 55% opacity under reduced motion.

motion.name: scheme-article-border-draw
motion.value: scheme-elevation-draw 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) backwards; +70ms per plant; flower heads: scheme-elevation-dot 0.4s ease, one beat later
motion.purpose: The scheme article's authored moment: on arrival each plant's silhouette in the masthead draws up from the ground line (stroke-dashoffset on pathLength-normalised paths), its flower heads budding in the plant's own colour a beat later. Nothing else on the page moves at rest; the closing band's copy of the border is drawn still.

breakpoints.name: scheme-article container: masthead and closing band side by side
scheme-article container: left rail, plants two abreast
scheme-article container: four seasons in a row

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action per view. Marigold fill, near-black ink-deep text (the pairing that clears AA), near-square corners.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Add plant</button>

components.name: Secondary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 2px); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; inline-size: max-content; cursor: pointer; background-color: transparent; color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); border: 1px solid var(--color-n-deep-grey); transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); border-color: var(--color-y-yellow); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-paper), 0 0 0 4px var(--color-p-lavender); } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Lowest-stakes inline action. No border; hover fills highlight-yellow.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost">Cancel</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 2px); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; inline-size: max-content; cursor: pointer; background-color: transparent; color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-paper), 0 0 0 4px var(--color-p-lavender); }

components.name: Scheme Button
components.description: The Planting Schemes context's own action colour — lavender fill, lavender-white text. Reserved for a scheme's own finishing actions (e.g. "Generate the scheme") so it never competes with marigold, which stays the one primary accent elsewhere on the same view (e.g. the chat composer's send button).
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-scheme"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M14 9.536V7a4 4 0 0 1 4-4h1.5a.5.5 0 0 1 .5.5V5a4 4 0 0 1-4 4 4 4 0 0 0-4 4c0 2 1 3 1 5a5 5 0 0 1-1 3"/><path d="M4 9a5 5 0 0 1 8 4 5 5 0 0 1-8-4"/><path d="M5 21h14"/></svg>Generate the scheme</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-scheme { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 2px); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; inline-size: max-content; cursor: pointer; background-color: var(--color-p-lavender); color: var(--color-p-white); transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-btn-scheme:hover { background-color: var(--color-o-vermillion); color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); } .ds-btn-scheme:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-paper), 0 0 0 4px var(--color-p-lavender); } .ds-btn-scheme:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field. Mono label above (.o-type-label — Spline Sans Mono, uppercase, 0.14em); paper fill, sand-line border, strong marigold focus (border, ring and fill all shift).
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.375rem; } .ds-field__label { font-family: var(--font-spline-mono), ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--color-ink-soft); } .ds-field__input { border: 1px solid var(--color-sand-line); border-radius: var(--radius-m, 4px); padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-ink); background-color: var(--color-paper); transition: background-color 150ms, border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-field__input::placeholder { color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink-soft) 50%, transparent); } .ds-field__input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-r-marigold); background-color: var(--color-r-marigold); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-paper), 0 0 0 3px var(--color-r-marigold); }

components.name: Toggle
components.description: A 44×24 pill switch (role=switch) with a 16px knob. Off is an outlined track (transparent fill, n-dark-grey border and knob); on is a filled track (cyan-deep) with a white knob — the two states differ by fill and knob position, never colour alone.
components.css: .ds-toggle-row { display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: center; } .ds-toggle { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; inline-size: 44px; block-size: 24px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-n-dark-grey); border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 32px); background-color: transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.4s ease, border-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-toggle__knob { position: absolute; inset-inline-start: 5px; inline-size: 16px; block-size: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background-color: var(--color-n-dark-grey); transition: transform 0.4s ease, background-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-toggle--on { background-color: var(--color-b-cyan-deep); border-color: var(--color-b-cyan-deep); } .ds-toggle--on .ds-toggle__knob { background-color: var(--color-white); transform: translateX(20px); }

components.name: Photo Dropzone
components.description: The add-a-plant photo well (`.c-add-photo`). A 172px band on the warm orange fill with a dashed marigold edge held in both rest and hover (the fill alone is too pale to define the zone); hover swaps the fill to highlight-yellow and softens the corner.
components.css: .ds-dropzone { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; inline-size: 100%; max-inline-size: 320px; block-size: 172px; border: 2px dashed var(--color-r-marigold); border-radius: var(--radius-s, 2px); background-color: var(--color-o-orange); color: var(--color-ink-soft); font-family: var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.73rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.4s ease, color 0.4s ease, border-radius 0.4s ease; } .ds-dropzone:hover { background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); border-radius: var(--radius-m, 4px); }

components.name: Radio Card
components.description: A photo card acting as one option in a picker (`.c-identify-option` / the garden-gallery multi-select tile). Selection can't be a fill on a photograph, so it's carried by a mark that is always drawn: an empty ring unchosen, a filled cyan-deep disc with a white check when chosen. Hover is the card lift only — the edge never borrows the selected treatment.
components.css: .ds-radio-row { display: flex; gap: 16px; } .ds-radio-card { position: relative; inline-size: 96px; block-size: 96px; border-radius: var(--radius-m, 4px); border: 1px solid var(--color-n-dark-grey); background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); overflow: hidden; transition: box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-radio-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); } .ds-radio-card--chosen { border-color: var(--color-b-cyan-deep); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-b-cyan-deep); } .ds-radio-card__media { inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; } .ds-radio-card__mark { position: absolute; inset-block-start: 8px; inset-inline-end: 8px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; inline-size: 18px; block-size: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background-color: var(--color-white); border: 2px solid var(--color-n-dark-grey); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-white); color: transparent; } .ds-radio-card--chosen .ds-radio-card__mark { background-color: var(--color-b-cyan-deep); border: 2px solid var(--color-white); color: var(--color-white); }

components.name: Trait Badge
components.description: Static, non-interactive label. Pill, 1px border, colour set per trait via the --sem-* semantic layer. Shown here in the 'edible' variant.
components.html: Edible
components.css: .ds-badge { --_bg: var(--color-paper); --_fg: var(--color-ink-soft); --_bd: var(--sem-border-color); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: var(--space-xs, 4px); border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 32px); border: 1px solid var(--_bd); background-color: var(--_bg); color: var(--_fg); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.85rem; line-height: 2; padding-inline: var(--space-sm, 8px); white-space: nowrap; width: max-content; } .ds-badge--edible { --_bg: var(--sem-edible-bg); --_fg: var(--sem-edible-fg); --_bd: var(--sem-edible-bg); } .ds-badge--sm { font-size: 0.65rem; line-height: 1.5; padding-inline: var(--space-xs, 4px); }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Interactive tag (filter / dismissible). Pill, asymmetric padding to seat a trailing circular action; hover warms to gold.
components.html: Foxglove
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: var(--space-xs, 4px); border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 32px); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.85rem; line-height: 2; padding-inline-start: var(--space-sm, 8px); padding-inline-end: var(--space-xs, 4px); white-space: nowrap; width: max-content; background-color: transparent; color: var(--color-ink-soft); transition: background-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-chip:hover { background-color: var(--color-y-gold); } .ds-chip__action { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 24px; width: 24px; padding: 0; border: none; border-radius: 50%; background-color: transparent; color: inherit; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-chip__action:hover { background-color: var(--color-white); }

components.name: Plant Card
components.description: The core content unit. White raised surface on grained paper, 4px corners, flat at rest, lifts on hover; 4:3 media well with badge slot. Bold-roman Zodiak title with the botanical binomial italicised (a pure-Latin title reads fully italic).
components.html:
Full sun

Digitalis purpurea

Foxglove
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; border-radius: var(--radius-m, 4px); background-color: var(--color-white); text-decoration: none; color: inherit; transition: box-shadow 150ms, transform 75ms, opacity 75ms; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); z-index: 1; } .ds-card:active { transform: scale(0.98); opacity: 0.75; } .ds-card__media { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); } .ds-card__badge { position: absolute; top: var(--space-xs, 4px); right: var(--space-xs, 4px); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 32px); border: 1px solid var(--sem-full-sun-bg); background-color: var(--sem-full-sun-bg); color: var(--sem-full-sun-fg); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.65rem; line-height: 1.5; padding-inline: var(--space-xs, 4px); } .ds-card__body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.375rem; padding: var(--space-md, 16px); flex: 1; } .ds-card__title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-fraunces), serif; font-style: italic; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-card__sub { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--color-ink-soft); }

components.name: Primary Nav
components.description: Equal-width tab strip under the app header. Transparent 2px bottom border; hover shows a marigold underline, active adds marigold text and medium weight.
components.html: HomePlantsSchemes
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-border-color); } .ds-nav__item { flex: 1; display: flex; justify-content: center; padding-top: var(--space-sm, 8px); margin-bottom: -1px; font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; text-decoration: none; color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 0.4s ease, border-bottom-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-nav__item:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--color-r-marigold); } .ds-nav__item--active { color: var(--color-r-marigold); border-bottom-color: var(--color-r-marigold); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Popover Menu
components.description: The single shared dropdown shell (user menu, scheme actions, plant filter). White, hairline border, 4px radius, low menu shadow; items fill highlight-yellow on hover, danger items fill smoke-red.
components.css: .ds-popover { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-sm, 8px); min-width: 200px; padding: var(--space-xs, 4px); background-color: var(--color-white); border: 1px solid var(--sem-border-color); border-radius: var(--radius-m, 4px); box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px #0000001a, 0 2px 4px -2px #0000001a; } .ds-popover__item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-sm, 8px); width: 100%; padding: var(--space-sm, 8px) var(--space-md, 16px); border: none; background-color: transparent; color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.4s ease; } .ds-popover__item:hover { background-color: var(--color-y-yellow); } .ds-popover__item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-b-cyan); } .ds-popover__item--danger:hover { background-color: var(--color-r-smoke-red); }

components.name: Chat Bubble
components.description: One turn in the c-chat conversation surface. Assistant bubbles on paper-deep (borderless), the person's on white with a hairline; each squares one corner toward its speaker. The 'Plotted' attribution with a sprout mark shows once at the head of an assistant run. Role is alignment + fill tone + attribution, never colour alone.
components.html:
Plotted
I'll help you turn this into a full planting scheme — ask for a swap, more options in a direction, or tell me what isn't working.
Full sun, mostly.

components.name: Typing Indicator
components.description: Shown in the c-chat log while the assistant composes a reply. Three dots in a paper-deep bubble; role=status with a visually-hidden 'Plotted is thinking'. The chat surface's one authored moment.

components.name: Chat Composer
components.description: The c-chat message input: an auto-growing textarea (field-sizing: content, repeated-entry focus — marigold ring + border, no fill flip, marigold caret) and a 44px roundel send button in the brand accent. Enter sends, Shift+Enter newlines.

components.name: Living Border Sheet
components.description: The head of the /plant-scheme/chat scheme list — the list drawn as a border taking shape, not a list. Under the season-washed letterhead: the border elevation (an engraved cross-section on a shared ground line — every tiered plant one silhouette in the path accent, a dashed ghost holding any empty tier) and the flowering year (twelve month cells filling with their season's --sem-flowering-* pair, a small accent tick under the current month). The elevation and year are held to a centred ~22rem figure measure so they stay diagram-scale on a wider sheet. New silhouettes draw themselves in on the emphasis curve — part of 'the planting' (see motion).
components.html:
Scheme list3 plants

components.name: Scheme Generate Action
components.description: The scheme-list pane's finishing action (SchemeGenerateAction.tsx, added alongside the /plant-scheme/chat workspace) — a plain-language line describing what "Generate the scheme" will do, pinned beneath the growing plant list on wide screens the same way the chat composer pins beneath its log. Completing swaps the button for a quiet confirmation in the path's own flowering-season accent, never a second button.
components.html: Happy with your border? We'll save these 6 plants and put together your planting guide — how to arrange them, and how to care for them through the year.
components.css: .ds-generate { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 16px; max-inline-size: 22rem; border-block-start: 1px solid var(--sem-border-color); } .ds-generate__lead { margin: 0; color: var(--color-ink-soft); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.81rem; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-generate__button { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; inline-size: 100%; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-s, 2px); font-family: var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; background-color: var(--color-p-lavender); color: var(--color-p-white); transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-generate__button:hover { background-color: var(--color-o-vermillion); color: var(--color-n-deep-grey); }

components.name: Order Book Letterhead
components.description: The shopping list's head (and its compact copy on the dashboard): the one dark field in the app. Dusk (damson lit by a low marigold glow and a mulberry lift), the title in blossom, one Zodiak-italic aside, and an engraved border with one silhouette per plant, dashed ghosts for ground still to plant, and a bird in gold. The shipped version also carries the specimen plates' grain. Scoped to the shopping list: see the Dusk Field exception.
components.html:

narrative.overview:
Plotted takes the rigour of a printed nursery plant catalogue — plate numbers, italic botanical Latin, hairline rules, warm paper stock, a faint printed grain — and pulls it forward into something brighter and unmistakably software. It is a knowingly AI-assisted gardening companion, so the surface is allowed to feel technical and tactile at the same time: real texture and warmth, but crisp edges and no nostalgic cosplay. The Nursery Catalogue is a reference for precision and calm, not for period styling.

Colour is drawn from the garden itself and used through the interface to echo that richness — sun needs, flowering seasons, plant traits all carry their own hue — but it is held in restraint so it never competes with the gardener's own plant photographs, which are always the brightest thing on the page. Chrome stays quiet; content brings the colour. The single brand accent, a warm marigold, is spent sparingly on primary action and active navigation.

The atmosphere to protect is alive, bright, warm, friendly, supportive; simple, informative, and never chaotic or clinical. Depth is achieved with tonal paper layers and 1px hairlines rather than shadow — surfaces are flat at rest, and a shadow only ever appears as a response to interaction.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#FAF6EC) with a faint multiply-blended noise grain — never flat white; white is reserved for raised cards.

Zodiak for every display and heading level — bold roman (600) in the product UI, italic 400 on marketing/editorial surfaces; Inter for UI text; Spline Sans Mono for labels, plate numbers and botanical metadata.
Structure carried by 1px hairline borders and paper/sand tonal layering; flat by default.
One brand accent (marigold) used on ≤10% of a screen; a broad --sem-* semantic-colour system carries all trait, sun, season and status colour.
Print-catalogue devices retained: specimen/plate numbers, italic Latin, caption lines, framed image "plates".
Two type-adjacent registers: a wide editorial marketing surface (~1120px) and a narrow product measure (~800px).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: **The One Accent Rule.** Marigold is the only brand accent in product chrome and appears on ≤10% of any screen — primary action and active nav. Anywhere the interface is more colourful than that, the colour is coming from plant *content* (photos, traits, seasons) via the semantic layer, not from chrome.

rules.name: The Semantic Layer Rule
rules.body: **The Semantic Layer Rule.** Trait, sun, season and status colours are declared as `--sem-*` tokens that reference the palette (or a purpose-made hex where the review demanded one). Components read `--sem-*` through object-private `--_*` custom properties — never raw `--color-*` — for any stateful colour. New state colours go through this layer.

rules.name: The Focus Colour Rule
rules.body: **The Focus Colour Rule.** Every focus ring and every active-field edge in the app reads `--sem-focus-color` — never `--color-b-cyan`, never a per-component value. It resolves to Cyan Deep because a focus indicator is a non-text UI component under WCAG 1.4.11 and must clear 3:1 against whatever it sits on; the app's grounds run from paper to highlight-yellow, so the token is chosen against the lightest of them. A new interactive object gets its focus state from this token, and if the indicator ever needs to change, it changes here once.

rules.name: The Highlight-Yellow convention
rules.body: **The Highlight-Yellow convention** *(established pattern, not an invariant).* `highlight-yellow` is the one reactive colour that marks whatever the pointer is on. Keep every new interactive object consistent with it on hover/active. It marks the pointer and **nothing else** — see the next rule.

rules.name: The Chosen-Is-Filled Rule
rules.body: **The Chosen-Is-Filled Rule.** In a choose-one group, hover and selected must never share a treatment. Hover takes the highlight-yellow tint; *chosen* takes a **fill** in the context's accent (lavender in Planting Schemes) with its paired light text. The failure this prevents is specific and was live in `.c-scheme-prefs__choice`: hover and `.is-selected` shared one declaration block, so moving the pointer across the group made every option you touched look like the one you had picked. A fill also survives sitting next to a hovered sibling, which a border-colour swap does not. Where the option is a **photo card**, a fill would bury the photograph, so the job passes to a real radio mark that is drawn in *both* states (see Radio card) and hover falls back to the card lift. Selection must additionally be exposed to assistive tech — `aria-pressed` on a button group, or real radio semantics.

rules.name: The Semantic Field exception
rules.body: **The Semantic Field exception** *(scoped to the `/plant-scheme` journey).* The flowering-season hues normally appear only in small badges and roundels — "held in restraint" per the Overview. The planting-scheme flow is the one sanctioned place a `--sem-flowering-*` pair carries **large surfaces and a whole path's accent**:

rules.name: The Dusk Field exception
rules.body: **The Dusk Field exception** *(scoped to the shopping list).* The second sanctioned large colour field in the app, and the only one that is dark: the order book's letterhead (`/shopping-list`), its compact copy on the dashboard, and the head of the purchase dialog wear **dusk** — damson lit by a marigold glow low on the far side and a mulberry lift in the near corner, under the specimen plates' grain (`@mixin order-book-dusk`, `_shopping-item.scss`). It exists because this page cannot lean on photographs (Wikimedia images are often missing), so the page itself has to bring the colour. Marigold appears inside the gradient as light, not as chrome, so the One Accent Rule's count is unaffected. Like the Semantic Field, this is one surface's licence: a third dark band elsewhere is drift.

rules.name: Decorative tint
rules.body: **Decorative tint** *(shopping list common-name badges only).* Common names on a shopping list entry are `.o-badge` pills in one of five soft tints (blossom, hay, peach, lavender-white, clay), picked from the name by hash. The tint carries **no meaning** — it is variety on a page without photographs — and it deliberately avoids every `--sem-flowering-*` and trait colour so a badge can never be misread as a season or a trait. Don't extend this to a surface where badges already encode something.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: **The Two-Register Rule.** Zodiak *headings* are **bold roman (600)** in the product UI and **italic (400)** on marketing/editorial surfaces — never mixed within one surface. An app section header in italic, or a marketing headline in bold roman, is drift. Weight and style are chosen by surface mode (Operate → roman 600; Persuade/Read editorial → italic 400), not by taste per screen.

rules.name: The Mono Label Rule
rules.body: **The Mono Label Rule.** Eyebrows, specimen/plate numbers, field labels and botanical metadata all use `.o-type-label` — Spline Sans Mono, uppercase, `letter-spacing: 0.14em`, weight 500, `.minion` size. One class, no per-context variants; it is the type element that carries the "tech-aware" half of the identity.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: **The One Scale Rule.** Type size comes only from the printers'-names step classes (`minion → canon` + `long-` variants) in `styles/base/_typography.scss`, and line-height only from `.o-type-leading--*`. Tailwind `text-*` / `font-*` / `leading-*` and arbitrary `text-[Npx]` are not part of this system — they are being converted out. Never introduce a new size value; map the need onto the nearest step.

rules.name: The Latin-in-Italic Rule
rules.body: **The Latin-in-Italic Rule.** Botanical names (genus, species, cultivar) are always rendered italic, whatever the surrounding type.

rules.name: The breakout device
rules.body: **The breakout device** — `.c-garden-gallery__grid` (the planting-scheme start panel's plant grid) only: a single element, not a page or container measure. `margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw)` escapes to the viewport edge, then `padding-inline: max(var(--space-md), calc(50vw - 38rem))` re-centres it at a `76rem` cap — wider than any page measure above, but scoped to one grid, not the page around it: the search field and "In your garden" heading immediately above it stay at the product measure, so the page visibly opens up right at the grid rather than the whole page widening. Below roughly `60rem` the formula floors back to the page's own `--space-md` gutter, so a phone sees no breakout at all. The same margin-trick the hub's retired first-run teaser used to use for its photo triptych — same mechanism, now spent on the real task (browsing a whole garden) instead of a marketing moment. See Planting schemes hub → Garden gallery.

rules.name: The Narrow Column Rule
rules.body: **The Narrow Column Rule.** App pages hold to the ~800px `.o-page` measure — one readable column, one task. The 1120px editorial container is a marketing device and never appears in the app. The **sanctioned width exception** is the dashboard, which runs the ~1000px companion measure (still one centred column, never multi-column) because it is a stack of peer check-in blocks rather than a single task. The `/plant-scheme/chat` workspace (below) is another, and the shopping list's order book measure (80rem, above) is the third — granted because buying plants turned out to be a primary job of the product, not a side list, and the page needed room to show two entries abreast. The finished scheme's article measure (76rem, above) is the fourth — granted because the page is where the scheme journey's wide workspace lands, and its figures (the border, the year in flower) and two-abreast plant entries need the room; its prose does not widen with it. The planting schemes hub (`/plant-scheme`) is no longer a third at the *page* level — it held a bounded two-column exception until a revision retired it in favour of a single column with a "Recent plans" preview, so full browsing/management could move to its own route (`/plant-scheme/plans`) instead of sharing the hub with the starting task. Its garden gallery grid does still break out, but as the breakout device (above) — one element opting itself wider, not the page or a container claiming a new measure — which is why it isn't a fourth page-level exception here. A new app route wanting extra width, at the page or container level, is drift, not a precedent; a single element with a real reason to bloom past its container is a different, and much cheaper, decision.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: **The Flat-By-Default Rule.** Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only as a reaction to state — hover, open, overlay — and never as ambient decoration. If a resting element needs to stand out, reach for a tonal layer or a hairline first.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: **The Grain Rule.** The page ground always carries its `feTurbulence` noise texture at ~8% alpha, `multiply` blended. A pure flat `#FFF` or un-grained `#FAF6EC` fill at page level is a regression.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: **The One Authored Moment Rule.** A surface gets one motion that is designed — orchestrated, on the emphasis curve, from an already-visible resting state. Everything else is incidental (default curve) or still. Every keyframe and transition honours `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — the authored moment degrades to an instant state change, never a jump.

dos: **Do** keep the page ground `#FAF6EC` *with* its noise grain (multiply, ~8%). White is for raised cards, dialogs and menus — and for the chat composer, the one field on a tinted surface that has to read as an unwritten page.
**Do** set product-UI headings in Zodiak bold roman (`.kirk` / 600); use Zodiak italic 400 only on marketing/editorial surfaces (the Two-Register Rule).
**Do** use Spline Sans Mono, uppercase, `0.12–0.16em` tracking for eyebrows, plate numbers, field labels and botanical meta.
**Do** render botanical Latin italic, always — including inside a bold-roman title, where it reads as bold-roman with an italic species.
**Do** carry structure with 1px hairlines (`--sem-border-color`) and tonal paper layers; add shadow only on hover / open / overlay.
**Do** route every stateful colour through a `--sem-*` token and an object-private `--_*` property — never a raw `--color-*` in a modifier.
**Do** keep marigold rare: primary action and active nav, ≤10% of a screen.
**Do** let colour enter through plant content — photos and the trait/sun/season badge families — while chrome stays calm.

**Do** treat the planting schemes hub (`/plant-scheme`) as a single-task page — start a scheme, with a light Recent plans glance above it. Its season-washed start panel belongs to the scheme journey; on another Operate screen it is drift. Full plan browsing and management belongs on `/plant-scheme/plans`, not folded back into the hub. "How it works" content belongs in the welcome dialog's `OnboardingCarousel`, shown once to a genuinely first-time gardener — not a standing disclosure on the hub.

**Do** carry the scheme's flowering-season accent through the conversation via `--_accent` / `--_accent-wash`, and reuse the journey chrome (`.c-scheme-journey` step marker, the border elevation, the tray pill) rather than reinventing it per screen.

**Do** hold app pages to the ~800px `.o-page` measure; the 1120px container is a marketing device, the ~1000px companion measure is the dashboard's alone, the 80rem order book measure is the shopping list's alone, the 76rem scheme article measure is the finished scheme's alone, and full width is the `/plant-scheme/chat` workspace's alone — the Layout section lists every exception. The planting schemes hub sits at the ordinary product measure now too.

**Do** build any new conversation on the `c-chat` primitives (`_chat.scss` / `ChatLog.tsx`) — a boxless internally-scrolling log with `role="log"` + `aria-live` (height capped via `--short` / `--bounded` or flexed to fill; `--bounded` foot-fades toward the composer), attribution once per run, a typing indicator before a reply, an auto-growing composer set a rhythm step off the log, focus back to the composer after send.

**Do** build a choose-one set as a *set* — full-width rows stacked in one column, label leading, a mark drawn in both states held to the trailing edge — and close it once the choice is made, so scrollback reads as a record rather than as live buttons (see Chat → Choose-one options).
**Do** take every focus ring and active-field edge from `--sem-focus-color` (Cyan Deep) — the light `--color-b-cyan` is a fill/selected tint and is too pale to be an indicator.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion` for every animation (all current keyframes already opt out).

**Do** give every async chat turn a real retry/discard path (`SendFailedNotice` in `ChatLog.tsx`) rather than letting a failure be silent — at most one turn in flight or failed at a time, composer/rows lock until it resolves, exactly two ways out.
**Do** hold every decision point in the chat to ≤4 visible options — split a longer suggestion panel into tier groups (`SuggestionPanel.tsx`) rather than presenting more at once.
**Do** give a closed choose-one group a way back (`.c-chat__options-reopen`) once it's genuinely committed — a permanent choice with no undo is a dead end, not a decision.

**Do** give each pane of a multi-pane layout a real landmark (`<section aria-label>` / `aria-labelledby`) rather than trying to make DOM tab order track pixel position — that only works for one column, and reordering or focus-trapping to chase it is worse than the mismatch itself.

**Do** pair that landmark with a `.u-skip-link` for keyboard-only users with no screen reader — landmarks are AT-specific and don't help them; a visually-hidden-until-focused `<a href="#…">` to a `tabIndex={-1}` section is the equivalent affordance.

**Do** say "(optional)" in an optional field's label, in sentence-case Inter after the mono label — don't leave it to be inferred from a missing asterisk, and don't hide optional fields behind a disclosure when there are only two of them.
**Do** draw a "mark this done" action with an **empty** mark at rest and a verb-led label ("Mark as bought"). A resting tick beside a past-tense label reads as a status.
**Do** keep a dialog open while its action runs and report a failure inside it, beside the thing it concerns — and open any destructive dialog with focus on the safe button.

**Do** tell the gardener what a background lookup is doing and how it ended: looking, no match, failed (with a way to try again), or resolved. An entry that silently shows nothing looks the same as one never looked up.

**Do** make a surface that can't rely on photographs carry its own colour and illustration (the order book's dusk letterhead, engraved border and specimen-plate monograms) rather than leaving grey placeholder wells.
donts: **Don't** give a plant without a photograph an empty frame or a monogram on the scheme article. That entry is set differently (no plate, its word-picture larger); the specimen plate is for surfaces where a media well is fixed, like a card grid.
**Don't** use a flower colour (`--_bloom`) for anything but that plant's bar, dot and flower heads, and don't add an eleventh without adding it to the prompt's list and the migration's check.

**Don't** reuse the order book's dusk letterhead, its engraved border, or the decorative badge tints on another route — they are the shopping list's (and its dashboard panel's), as the season washes are the scheme journey's.
**Don't** colour a shopping list badge with a flowering-season or trait colour; the tints there are deliberately meaningless.
**Don't** spread a shopping list entry into aligned columns with column heads — tried and retired; sparse entries leave the columns empty. Use the stacked entry and set entries side by side instead.
**Don't** introduce a third palette or bring the marketing `moss` / `terra` / `sage` greens into product UI — `styles/abstracts/_variables.scss` is the single source of truth.
**Don't** use `--color-ink` for body copy — running text is `--color-n-deep-grey`; `ink` / `ink-soft` are for headings and labels.
**Don't** drift toward the plant-ID app look: no dark UI, neon accents, camera-first chrome, or gamified score badges. The "N/12 spotted" hook is a gentle prompt, not a scoreboard.
**Don't** drift twee: no script or hand-lettered fonts, watercolour blobs, floral borders, or pastel whimsy.
**Don't** set essential copy over a photograph — captions and copy sit beside or below the image (see Shapes → image plate).

**Don't** copy the hub's start-panel washes, the drafts' elevation thumbnails or the annotated example onto another app route — they belong to the scheme journey, not the app at large (see Planting schemes hub).

**Don't** give chat bubbles a marigold (or any accent) fill, or lean on colour alone to tell assistant from user — the split is alignment + fill tone + the attribution line. Keep the season accent on the *wrapper* chrome (`--_accent` on the workspace/list), never inside `c-chat`.
**Don't** mix heading registers within a surface — no italic-400 section header inside the app, no bold-roman headline on a marketing page.
**Don't** add dashboards, KPI tiles, stat walls or streak counters (a PRODUCT.md commitment).
**Don't** put `--color-b-cyan` on a focus ring, a focus outline or an active-field border — that is `--sem-focus-color`'s job (the Focus Colour Rule).

**Don't** let a control's boundary get *weaker* when it reacts. Three controls shipped with a hover that swapped a defined edge for pale cyan or for the hover fill itself, leaving the hovered state with less definition than the resting one. Where the highlight-yellow hover also takes the border, the control must already carry a fill at rest; a transparent or lightly-tinted control keeps its edge and changes only the fill.

**Don't** set a control label in Zodiak. The display face is the heading voice; on a button or an option plate it makes the control read as a card title — as content rather than as something to pick. Inter `--font-weight-medium` is the label voice for controls.

**Don't** use `--color-r-marigold` for error text on paper — it clears only ~3:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor for body-sized text. Use `--sem-color-error-bg` for inline error copy instead (see the Failed turn entry under Chat).

**Don't** reach for `role="radiogroup"` on options that act on click. Arrow keys in a radiogroup move the selection, which there means firing a request per keypress; a labelled `role="group"` of `aria-pressed` buttons is the honest shape and owes no roving tabindex.

**Don't** build a click target as a `div` with `onClick`. Every one of them in this codebase turned out to be the only path to its action, with no tab stop, no accessible name and nowhere to put a focus state.
**Don't** hardcode radius, spacing or colour values — use the scale tokens; Stylelint checks them.
**Don't** put a resting shadow on a surface to make it "pop" — use a tonal step or a hairline.
**Don't** touch `styles/objects/plant-detail.scss` or the `.plant` / `.plant-detail` / `.plant__frost-tolerance` selectors — they're fenced off for a dedicated refactor.
**Don't** add new component CSS as `components/ui/*.module.css` — global SCSS/ITCSS (`styles/objects/`, `styles/components/`) is the settled architecture.
